name: Five Whys
description: Follow a chain of contributing conditions, checking each link and stopping claims where the evidence stops.

walkthroughIntro.inOneLine: Follow a chain of contributing conditions, checking each link and stopping claims where the evidence stops.
walkthroughIntro.bestFor: A recurring, observable failure whose contributing causes need checking.
walkthroughIntro.howLong: 36 minutes for 2–6 participants; also available solo.
walkthroughIntro.origin: An independently written workflow using a widely known thinking method. Instructions and fictional examples were created for this app; no third-party endorsement is claimed.

lenses.name: Why did this outcome occur?
lenses.instruction: Name the immediate condition that could explain the outcome. Cite an observation or record. Keep an alternative explanation alongside it.

lenses.name: What produced that condition?
lenses.instruction: Choose a supported link from the first reveal and ask what made that condition possible. Name the earlier answer you are building on and the evidence for this link.

lenses.name: What sustained the pattern?
lenses.instruction: Ask what contributed to the condition in the second reveal. Separate a recurring system condition from a one-time event. If evidence has run out, describe the missing check instead of inventing a cause.

lenses.name: Check another link or branch
lenses.instruction: Investigate one more supported link, or return to an alternative explanation. State what observation would contradict your current causal chain.

lenses.name: Choose a cause to investigate or change
lenses.instruction: Review the chain. Identify one contributing condition within reach, its evidence, and a check that could disprove it. Five questions are a guide, not a requirement to claim a single root cause.

blocks.title: Agree the question
blocks.prompt: Describe one observed outcome, when it occurred and how often. Avoid naming a person as the cause. Agree which records the group can inspect.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group agrees the question and boundaries before contributing.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A shared question keeps the later comparisons relevant.

blocks.title: Choose the next step
blocks.prompt: State the supported causal chain, the unresolved alternative, and the next check or small intervention. Do not call an untested explanation the root cause.

criteria.text: The conclusion links at least two contributing conditions to the observed outcome.

scoring.zero: No explanatory chain connects conditions to the outcome.
scoring.one: One contributing condition is linked, or multiple conditions are listed without connecting them.
scoring.two: At least two contributing conditions are connected to the outcome, e.g. an unassigned queue delayed routing, which delayed replies.

criteria.text: Observed evidence is distinguished from an unverified explanation.

scoring.zero: A guessed explanation is stated as fact without supporting observations.
scoring.one: Evidence is mentioned but which part of the explanation remains unverified is unclear.
scoring.two: Observed evidence and an unverified link are separated, e.g. timestamps show a delay; lack of ownership is still a hypothesis.

criteria.text: An alternative explanation and a concrete verification step are included.

scoring.zero: No alternative or verification step is provided.
scoring.one: An alternative or a check is named, but not both or not connected.
scoring.two: An alternative explanation is named and a concrete check can distinguish it from the proposed chain.

walkthrough.whatHappens: Participants propose and vote on a conclusion. Review checks the method-specific criteria; solo sessions can use the same checklist.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A choice should explain its reasoning and limits.

blocks.title: Assign the follow-through
blocks.prompt: Choose an owner, first action, due date and observable success signal.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group assigns one person the first action and records when and how to check it.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: An owner and a check make the conclusion actionable.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The engine saves the contributions, conclusion and commitment as reports.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: The record makes assumptions and follow-through available for review.
